observations: Forced ride: steer/jump/dash only, no backtracking, so crate placement is lane choice plus jump timing and every miss is permanent.
Groups of 1-5 crates about one per screen, separated by hazard beats; per-section counts 12/15/17/7.
S1 alternates crate lanes L-R-L before the first two-sided hazard asks for the same tempo.

Three towers, one prop (worker-held springboard), three answers: ignore / bounce / jump over; crates sit in the tunnel / on the roof / under the tower; loose lives on the wrong-answer roofs are decoys.
Two of three life crates float above the road - the count traps of the stage.
Every checkpoint is embedded in a crate group (W-C-W, slalom head, W+C).
Time crates total 29 s against a 16.9 s record: in time trial the crates are the race.
Pura crouches before jumps and on landing: time crates on stack tops need a landing timed just before the stack (TT fr.10).
Dash dissolves hazards (barrels, low dragons, crevices) but not the steering demand of the crate lines.

geometryObservations: **A reading test on a forced ride.** Steer, jump and dash are the only verbs, and nothing can be beaten (F3 p026R: dodge only; dodging sideways is more reliable than jumping). Geometry and enemies are hurdles to read, not fights.

**Holes never close the road.** Each break is cut from one parapet across half to two thirds of the width, so steering is the default answer and a jump the fallback; at full dash small crevices need no jump at all (P3), so speed removes the geometry.

**Teaching order:** a lateral jog (steer) → crates alternating sides → a staggered hole pair with a cart after it → static workers to one side → dragon 1 alone → dragon–hole–dragon → high dragons behind a crest → alternating heights near the crystal.

**The dragon height code.** Dragons 1–5 lie low (jump), 6–7 fly high (duck), then 8 over, 9 under, 10 under, 11 over. The first switch hides behind a blind hill crest; the alternation comes where the crystal distracts.

**Over-jumping is punished as much as under-jumping.** F3 forbids big jumps where traps follow each other (a monster may wait on the landing), and callout 3 places a hole exactly where a big jump over dragon 2 lands. Small hops are the norm.

**Combinations are short and spaced.** Hole + cart (S1), dragon + hole + dragon (S2), crest + high dragons + crack + springboard (S3), hole + springboard + tower wall (S4); clean stretches with crate groups lie between them.

**Towers are chokes and decision props.** Each squeezes the lane into a ≈3–4 u tunnel with a board on one side; B and C put a hole right before the board, so the decision is made while recovering from a hop.
**Static blockers stand beside crates.** Block-lifters and pole assistants occupy one half of the road next to crate pairs; the pole’s long reach makes a close sideways dodge the danger.
**Barrels come parked and rolling.** Carts are lane blocks against one parapet, often staggered left then right; loose barrels roll down slopes at you, and the dash breaks them.
**Slopes change timing.** Floating crates hang over a descending stepped road, a crate on an uphill must be jumped at the moment of contact (TT 22), and uphill jumps are short (cap. 05).
**Checkpoints on clean straights right after a read:** C1 after dragon 1, C2 after dragon 4 at the head of the slalom, C3 after dragons 10–11, each embedded in a crate row.
**The record line uses the same geometry differently:** parapet tops as landing strips over holes (cap. 03, 11), barrels blasted at speed, and the tower roof as the place of the 3-s crate.
geometryTransfer: **Half-width breaks on a fast lane.** On a 5–7 m road (4–6 u) with 0.8–1.15 m parapets, cut `pit` notches 2.5–3.5 m across and 1.2–2.3 m along from alternate sides, 4–6 m apart, with a parked obstacle beyond the second: at cruise a carve clears them, and a full ollie (9.4 m from cruise) is the fallback. Keep the parapets grindable as the expert line.

**Height-coded hurdles after a crest.** Use a low full-width sweeper (jump) five times, then, just past a blind crest, a `pendulum` or bar whose bob passes 2–3 m up — above head height (0.92 m) but inside a full-jump arc (2.85 m), so jumping into it is the mistake. Then alternate low and high.

**One prop, three answers.** Three `trampoline` towers on one line: A — crates in the low tunnel lane and a decoy pickup on the roof; B — a short hole, the trampoline (16 m/s launch, ≈3.8 m apex; ≈5.9 m held) and three crates on a roof 3.5–4.5 m up; C — a hole plus trampoline that a dash or charged ollie clears in one go, with crates in the tunnel beyond.

**Rolling barrels on slopes.** A `stone` (radius ≤ 0.7 m, so a full ollie at 1.78 m clears it) rolling down an uphill lane toward the rider, with parked blocks staggered left and right 10–15 m apart on the flat after it.

**Long-reach static guards beside crate pairs.** A `spinner` (2.1 m wide when its blades are out, 2.2 s out / 1.35 s in) 1.5–2 m from a crate pair at the road edge plays the pole assistant: a close pass times the blades, a wide pass leaves the crates.
